market_context: U.S. equities are staging a rebound after Thursday’s historic technology-led selloff linked to concerns that new congressional control could constrain AI data-center construction. October payrolls exceeded expectations at 165000 versus 65000, while wages rose 0.4% and unemployment fell to 4.1%, supporting equities but lifting the 10-year yield to 4.85% and limiting rate-sensitive technology upside. Intraday breadth favors semiconductors and high-beta growth, although the sharp rebound after the prior collapse raises late-session profit-taking risk.

predictions.reasoning: SPY is already up 0.87% after closing Thursday at $733.00, and the broader market is recovering from the prior session’s roughly 4.4% decline. Stronger-than-expected payroll growth and a sharply lower VIX support continued stabilization, though the 4.85% 10-year yield should restrict the magnitude of the advance.

QQQ has rebounded 1.94% from Thursday’s 6.49% collapse, with the Nasdaq-100 having suffered its worst session since 2020. The strong jobs report pushed Treasury yields higher, while the prior day’s AI-regulation shock remains unresolved; those factors favor afternoon consolidation or profit-taking after the early bounce.

Nvidia is up 3.62% after falling more than 9% Thursday, consistent with an oversold rebound after a reported 20.8% monthly decline. The stock remains below its intraday high near $194.90, and elevated yields plus unresolved concerns about AI infrastructure regulation create a risk of giving back part of the recovery.

Tesla has bounced 4.61% after an approximately 11% prior-session decline tied to regulatory concerns affecting Musk-linked companies. The rebound is stronger than the broad market and is vulnerable to late-session selling, particularly with the stock still down about 10% over five sessions.

DIA is comparatively resilient, nearly unchanged on the day after Thursday’s broad selloff, while the stronger payroll report supports economically sensitive large-cap shares. Its lower technology exposure than QQQ should reduce profit-taking pressure, favoring a modest close above the snapshot price.
